name: checkstyle
description: Checkstyle is a development tool to help programmers write Java code that adheres to a coding standard. By default it supports the Google Java Style Guide and Sun Code Conventions, but is highly configurable. It can be invoked with an ANT task and a command line program.
one_liner: A long-established tool that automatically checks whether Java code follows a consistent coding standard.
buyer: Honestly, this already has its buyer: it's free, mature infrastructure already embedded in most Java build pipelines — there's no fresh commercial opening here.
business_use_cases: Teams already use it for free as part of standard Java CI pipelines; there's no new use case to sell.
A consultancy could bundle Checkstyle configuration into a broader 'set up our CI pipeline' onboarding service, but that's a sliver of a larger engagement, not a business built on this tool.

money_ideas.idea: No realistic new revenue angle — it's mature, free, and widely adopted already.

steal_this: There's nothing to steal here — it's a 20-year-old free dev-tooling project doing its job well, not a business opportunity.
